newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks seen up on momentum, peso weaker.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks seen up on momentum, peso weaker.

text.p: --Mexico stocks seen edging up on momentum, Dow Jones
--Peso likely weak on foreign month-end dollar demand
--Cetes overnight rate viewed up on soft peso

Traders saw stocks opening with mild upside potential on Tuesday, bolstered by momentum from last week's gains, likely falls in primary interest rates and expected gains on Wall Street as investors return from the Memorial Day holiday.
"The market is firm, trading was not so bad yesterday, considering U.S. investors were absent and we had screen trading only," one desk trader said.

Traders expected the peso to open weak with month-end demand for dollars becoming heavier with foreign investors back in the market. Predicted falls in primary interest rates would also pressure the peso, they said.
Dealers forecast a trading range of 7.9100/9400 per dollar for the 48-hour peso. Pre-open bids stood at 7.9230/7.9270 per dollar, compared to Monday's close of 7.9130/7.9160.
Overnight rates on Cetes would likely open up from Monday's close of 17.10 percent, traders said, on a soft peso and on a weak U.S. 30-year Treasury bond, which was down 13/32 to yield 7.02 percent.
